PLA PPU1.5 Prefill E2E Accuracy and Performance Report

GDN/KDA performance comparison under current production semantics, plus historical FlashQLA optimization experiments.

Methodology: shapes are parsed from the raw caselist by the in-repo authoritative parser tests/utils.py (read_cmds_from_file / resolve_cu_seqlens), exactly as the test runner does; both sides share the same input tensors, indexed FP32 state pool, slot indices and cu_seqlens, and each call clones its own copy of the pool. Timing takes the CUDA Event median, warmup=5, repeat=20, dtype bfloat16, head_dim = 128. Speedup is Triton ms / PLA ms; >1 means PLA is faster.

Accuracy gate: KDA keeps the criterion of bench_vs_fla.py: assert_close(atol=0.02, rtol=0.01). The output/state relative L2 errors in the table are diagnostics, not the pass criterion: KDA outputs are small in magnitude, so the L2 ratio can still reach the 1e-2 range when element-wise assert_close passes.

Environment: na131t-swu116.eng.t-head.cn, device PPU-ZW810E (each caselist collected in parallel on its own card), PyTorch 2.10.0, Python 3.12.3, commit unknown, collected at 2026-09-15 14:52:17 +0800.

Reproduce:

for f in caselist/prefill/GLM-5.3-Flash_prefill_tp*.list \
         caselist/prefill/Kimi-K3_prefill_tp16_*.list; do
  tag=$(basename "$f" | sed 's/_kvlimit.*//')
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=$i python3 scripts/prefill/collect_bench_vs_fla.py \
      --caselist "$f" --select all --warmup 5 --repeat 20 \
      --output "reports/caselist/${tag}.json" &
  i=$((i+1))
done; wait
python3 scripts/prefill/generate_caselist_report_section.py \
    --input reports/caselist --html reports/perf_report_prefill.html \
    --csv reports/perf_prefill_caselist.csv --date 2026-09-14 ZW810E

810E replay (25/26 caselists, Kimi tp16 still missing; the 5 GLM lists were re-measured on 2026-09-15 on idle GPUs with the same methodology (--select all --warmup 5 --repeat 20)). Note: KDA (Kimi-K3 / GLM-5.3-Flash) on ZW810E has a median speedup of only ~0.05x (GDN is normal). The 2026-09-15 hgobjdump ISA attribution (--arch=ppu1.0 --line-numbers) shows the bf16 hardware conversion instructions are present as expected; 97% of the extra scalar instructions come from the c-fragment→b-fragment layout conversion lane scan at flashkda_ppu_util.cuh:347 -- PPU1.0 lacks PPU1.5's movmatrix hardware transpose instruction and can only take the 32×8×8 shuffle/compare fallback path. This is the kernel's established implementation on tc01, not a build regression, and rebuilding the wheel will not help; this data does not represent the kernel's level on PPU1.5.

GDN Prefill full acceptance: FLA-Triton vs PLA (2026-09-02)

lists / cases covered16 / 20,890
Accuracy passed20,890 / 20,890
Cumulative-time speedup1.776x
PLA faster (confirmed)20,890 / 20,890

Conclusion: all 20,890 cases pass accuracy and are all faster than FLA-Triton. The FLA-Triton/PLA cumulative device time is 78,263.972/44,079.855 ms, cumulative speedup 1.776x, per-case median speedup 1.713x, minimum speedup 1.0615x.

Method: the gate uses the FlashQLA benchmark's logsigmoid(randn) / 16, with 75% of heads slow-decay and the other 25% zero-decay; beta = sigmoid(randn). Both sides run through the same SGLang chunk_gated_delta_rule() entry, only toggling the PLA switch and sharing the inputs and the indexed FP32 state pool; the device time of that entry is taken as the CUDA Event median. The maximum output/state relative L2 errors are 6.134e-3/5.265e-3.

Current GDN prefill 13-shape standard set: FLA-Triton vs PLA (2026-08-28)

Accuracy passed13 / 13
PLA faster13 / 13
Median speedup1.749x
Total-time speedup1.722x

Summary: current PLA is faster than FLA-Triton on all 13 standard GDN prefill shapes; median speedup 1.749x, geomean 1.692x, range 1.441–1.785x. The FLA-Triton/PLA total-time ratio over the 13 shapes is 1.722x.

Origin of the 13 shapes: they are a hand-written standard set in the comparison script, not a full enumeration of caselist/prefill/. The latter currently has 20 lists and 26,266 records, of which GDN is 16 lists and 20,890 records; this table can therefore only be called the "13-shape standard set". The next section gives the independent results of the new runner executing FLA-Triton and PLA on every one of the 26,266 records; the two methodologies are not mixed.

Methodology: both sides run through the same SGLang chunk_gated_delta_rule() production entry, only toggling SGLANG_SAIL_PLA_PREFILL; inputs, indexed FP32 state pool, slot indices, cu_seqlens and pool clone are identical. Each shape runs in its own Python process, interleaving FLA-first/PLA-first, warmup=10, repeat=50; the table shows the median over 8 ZW-M890P cards on eu95t-swu264.eng.t-head.cn. All 104/104 executions passed the accuracy gate, with 0 foreign PPU PIDs.

Version under test: the current optimize_remove_unneeded_b_transpose candidate; FlashQLA extension SHA-256 is a736d0cda2c6c41a67635009c6137c47d675bd594f9ea589755baea557a773c1, current CP planner SHA-256 is df157a00735eb556bf03ad227bd2d5223ea6539cff3e18fa706d397978a1cc24; the planner signature of none of the 13 shapes in this table changed. Conclusion: current PLA is faster than FLA-Triton in cumulative time on all 20 lists. The FLA-Triton/PLA cumulative median times over the 26,266 records are 116,265.089 ms/64,435.178 ms, weighted speedup 1.804x, PLA cumulative time reduced by 44.579%. Of this, GDN is 1.703x and KDA is 1.990x.

Per-record methodology: the runner executes the SGLang production FLA-Triton entry and the current PLA entry separately for each record; both sides share the same inputs and clone the same indexed FP32 state pool inside their respective timed calls. The full test uses 72 shards on 8 cards, interleaving FLA-first/PLA-first by global index, warmup=2, repeat=5, timed by CUDA Event median. The test machine is the exclusive 30.70.218.2 (sz01t-swu450.eng.t-head.cn), with 0 foreign PPU PIDs over 6,225 audit cycles and all 8 cards idle before and after the test; the cumulative values in the table are the sums of the median times of all cases in each list.

FlashQLA PPU1.5 prefill: prepare_h register-B recompute experiment (2026-07-26)

Change: adds the PH_REG_GVD_RECOMPUTE=1 experimental path in prepare_h. FlashQLA PPU1.5 prefill: fused_fwd GEMM5 Vd register-B movmatrix transpose experiment (2026-07-27)

Change: adds acc16_to_bfrag_movmatrix_u32 on the FF_VD_REG_B experimental path, emulating movmatrix(src, warp_id) with a per-warp shared scratch: each warp writes the uint32 registers of its 32 threads linearly into shared memory, then reads back the transposed B-fragment via ppu.tc02.ldmatrix.sync.aligned.m8n8.x1.trans.shared.b16, replacing the original __shfl_sync c→b vregister transpose.

Build and accuracy: the remote PPU build passes (BUILD_RC=0), showing the current hggccc accepts this ppu.tc02.ldmatrix x1 trans instruction; full E2E accuracy passes, Dispatch 10/10, GVA 9/9, CP-path 5/5, h0 3/3, total 27/27 ALL PASS.

So turning on FF_VD_REG_B is still not recommended; the default stays 0, and the movmatrix helper is kept as the experimental basis for later lower-recompute / lower-register-pressure variants.
